output.answer: The closest result runs did not test 7.5% oxygen: at the same stated pressure, one recorded no ignition at 13.6% oxygen, while runs at 14.8–15.4% recorded flames that were extinguished or blew off [bass-ii-o12] [bass-ii-o4] [bass-ii-o9] [bass-ii-o11]. output.crew: At the lowered air, the provided oxygen partial pressure is 1.1 psi, equivalent by the app's standard-atmosphere arithmetic to 7,900 m, in the “Dangerous for crew” band. Less oxygen makes breathing harder; at 0% oxygen nothing can burn, and nobody can breathe it either.
output.instead: The evidence includes flames going out when airflow was reduced or turned off, including a PMMA run whose notes say it went out when the fan was off [bass-asrun-90-row100]; in microgravity, ventilation can feed a flame, so reducing airflow is a more directly supported response than relying on cabin oxygen dilution. To resolve the oxygen question, the needed test is a solid-fuel run at 7.5% oxygen and 14.7 psi.
